title: A code item's land.end row says lane=content, and ops prints land.end before the last land.step it shares a timestamp with
goal: Found in backlog.py ops SP-x5gjv4r7 at the review: each code item landed with --wait-merge (ST-yeymcu7l, ST-732j5ufa, ST-xuhig3u6, ST-ylje2dxh, BG-bgnkzjzt, ST-ifljijni, ST-mti4zrzz) has one land.end row with lane=content, the lane of its second pass (bl_land sets LAND_OPS lane per pass), so the row does not say the item's code went through a code/<id> merge request; and for ST-mbqowj5u and ST-ylje2dxh the land.end row and the final kbgit.py-sync-push land.step carry the same timestamp and ops prints the end first. A wait-merge landing's land.end names the code lane, and ops keeps a run's end after its steps.

run: import sys;t=open('_tools/bl_land.py',encoding='utf-8').read();sys.exit(1 if 'LAND_OPS["lane"] = "code" if late else "content"' in t else 0)

repro_reason: the lane is set in the second pass of a land run, which is reached only after a forge merge request merges; no planted root reaches it offline
